newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares end lower, Unibank extends gains.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares end lower, Unibank extends gains.

text.p: The Latvian market's sites remained trained on Unibanka on Wednesday as it extended recent gains, but dealers expect it to fall next week when one million of its shares are auctioned by the state.
Overall market volume on Wednesday was 103,000 lats and the Rietumu index eased 0.21 to 150.54. Three of the five official list stocks quoted on Wednesday gained while two held steady.

Dealers said the market, which lacks large institutional investors, was focused on domestic factors and unmoved by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks that U.S. economic growth had moderated.
Unibanka accounted for half of the session's turnover in trade of 55,700 lats as it rose to 3.25 lats from 3.23 lats.

The bank has been steadily inching up after falling sharply to 3.10 lats from 3.36 lats after the privatisation agency announced that one million of the state's shares would be auctioned for a minimum 3.05 lats on July 28.
Dealers said it appears that someone is supporting the price and it is expected to fall when the auction is held next Monday.
On the secondary list, pharmaceutical maker Olainfarm plummetted to 2.13 lats from 2.50 lats in trade of 4,500 lats.
Dealers said that it was only a matter of time before the stock, which seemed to have been supported at over 2.50 lats, fell. -- Ed Stoddard, Riga newsroom +371 722 66 93
